issues.description: process_frame complects payload-building, AWS client lifecycle, transport parsing, and frame bookkeeping in one async method
issues.detail: A single method opens an AWS client, decides multi-part vs single, splits SSE lines, strips prefixes, transforms text, and manages start/end frame bookends with a timer. These are four separable concerns: payload construction (pure), transport invocation (effect), event-stream parsing (pure), and response-segmentation (stateful). Decompose into pure functions over values and an effectful edge.

issues.description: output-response bookends complect identity, value, and time via mutable flags and a racing timer task
issues.detail: _output_response_open, _last_text_frame_time, and _close_task encode 'is a response currently open' as three coupled mutable places, with a 1.0s sleep racing against the final close in process_frame. The state machine is implicit and place-oriented. Model the response as a value (segment with start/end) and let one owner decide closure, not a flag plus a timer plus a final-block check.

issues.description: a fresh AWS client is constructed per invocation inside process_frame, complecting connection lifecycle with request handling
issues.detail: async with self._aws_session.client(...) on every LLMContextFrame ties client setup/teardown to a single message. That is incidental complexity from convenience: identity of 'the agentcore client' is conflated with the value of 'this one call'. Construct the client once at start, close at stop; keep request handling pure over that handle.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer will raise on any non-JSON line instead of returning None
issues.detail: json.loads(response_line) has no try/except; a malformed SSE line will propagate out of the transformer and abort the stream. The signature already says Optional[str]; honor it. Treat 'unparseable line' as a value (None) like the rest of the function, so the parsing loop stays simple and total.

issues.description: agentArn parameter uses camelCase, breaking PEP 8 and the surrounding snake_case API
issues.detail: Every other kwarg is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region). agentArn is easy because it mirrors the AWS field name, but it is not simple inside this codebase's vocabulary. Rename to agent_arn; map to agentRuntimeArn at the call site where the AWS wire format actually matters.

issues.description: os.getenv fallbacks for AWS credentials duplicate what aioboto3 already does and hide the credential-resolution chain
issues.detail: boto3/aioboto3 already resolves env vars, shared config, and instance metadata when arguments are None. Reading AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET/SESSION manually short-circuits that chain and freezes credentials at init time, breaking refresh for assumed roles. Pass None through and let the SDK own credential identity-over-time.

review.summary: The processor works but is COMPLECTED: process_frame braids payload construction, AWS client lifecycle, SSE parsing, and response-bookend bookkeeping into one async method, and the bookend state machine is PLACE-ORIENTED (a bool, a timestamp, and a racing close task all encoding the same fact). The pure pieces — context-to-payload, line-to-text, multi-part detection — want to be small total functions over values, with the effectful client at the edge and one explicit segmentation owner. Credential handling reaches around aioboto3's own resolution chain, which is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE and will bite on credential refresh. The question that should have been asked first: what is a 'response segment' here as a value, and who owns its start and end?
